title: Bayon Temple, Angkor Thom
summary: The Bayon was the state temple of the Khmer king Jayavarman VII, who after the Cham sack of Angkor in 1177 founded a new capital at Angkor Thom and began an unprecedented building campaign. ICOMOS calls the Buddhist temple towering; a visitor guide dates it to the late 12th or early 13th century.

uncertainty.note: No source opened gives the Bayon's own construction dates. ICOMOS places Jayavarman VII's building campaign after the sack of Angkor in 1177 and puts his death around 1200; a Siem Reap guide says it was begun in the late 12th or early 13th century. Start 1177 is only a lower bound. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: culminating in 1177 with the sack of Angkor by the Chams

when.display: Built under Jayavarman VII, c. late 12th to early 13th century; ruins stand today

where.modern_name: Bayon Temple, Angkor Thom, Siem Reap Province, Cambodia
where.historical_name: The Bayon, state temple of Jayavarman VII at Angkor Thom, Khmer Empire

importance.justification: ICOMOS names the Bayon among the masterpieces of the Angkor group and as Jayavarman VII's state temple.

The UNESCO list page for Angkor and the ICOMOS evaluation do not date the Bayon itself; the start year is a lower bound set by the 1177 sack, and the date is the weakest part of this record.
